executive_summary: Copenhagen's KPIs are all on target this month — occupancy, RevPAR, Revenue per FTE, and GOP % all landed in line with Budget. The one thing pulling GOP below Budget in dollar terms is the annual insurance premium and audit fee, both invoiced as a single January charge — expected every year, not an operating concern.
profitability_summary: GOP came in at 1,405,709 DKK, 3.1% (45,306 DKK) below Budget. The gap traces entirely to Property & Liability Insurance and Administrative & General, both carrying their annual January lump sum — strip those out and the underlying month is on target.

category_narratives.insurance: Insurance landed at roughly 12x its flat monthly Budget allocation — this is the annual Property & Liability Insurance premium, invoiced as a single January charge every year. Expected, not a concern; Budget is spread evenly across the year rather than matching the actual invoicing pattern.
category_narratives.admin_general: Administrative & General ran 18.3% over Budget, driven by the external audit fee that lands alongside the insurance premium each January (see above). No action needed — this is the same annual invoicing pattern, not a new cost.
category_narratives.total_undistributed_expenses: The undistributed-expense total is over Budget for the same reason as Administrative & General above — the January insurance/audit timing, not a broader cost trend.
category_narratives.gop: GOP is 3.1% below Budget this month, but the entire gap is explained by the January insurance/audit timing above — excluding that, the property is tracking to plan.
category_narratives.total_fixed_charges: Fixed charges are elevated for the same reason as Insurance above — the annual premium, not a new recurring cost.
category_narratives.ebitda: Follows GOP's variance for the same reason — the January insurance/audit timing flows straight through. Not an independent story.
category_narratives.ebit: Same driver as GOP/EBITDA above — no separate action needed here.
category_narratives.pretax_income: Same driver as GOP/EBITDA/EBIT above — no separate action needed here.
category_narratives.spa_other_exp: Spa & Wellness Other Expenses ran 3.2% over Budget — a small, immaterial variance on a small-dollar category. Worth a glance at the transaction detail next month if it repeats, not an action item on its own.
